sources.entry: iSimulator - iSimulator is a GUI utility to control the Simulator and manage the app installed on the simulator.

summary.one_liner: iSimulator is a macOS GUI utility for controlling iOS/watchOS/tvOS simulators and managing the apps installed on them.
summary.what_it_does: The app lists all simulators, including iOS, watchOS, tvOS and paired watches, and lets you create, erase, delete, pair, start and shut down simulators, with several able to run at once. For apps installed on a simulator, it shows the list, opens the app bundle and sandbox folder (it creates a folder containing both for easier access), and can launch, terminate or uninstall apps. It can also launch an app on a different simulator without rebuilding. The README says the list refreshes automatically when simulators or apps are added or removed.
use_cases: manage iOS simulators from a GUI
open an app's sandbox folder on the simulator
copy a built app to another simulator without rebuilding
pair an iPhone simulator with a watch simulator
launch, terminate or uninstall simulator apps
how_to_run: Download the App and run it.
If simulators are missing, set the active developer directory: sudo xcode-select -s <path>, or in Xcode go to Preferences -> Locations -> Command line tools.
notable: Creates a folder holding each app's bundle and sandbox for easy access
Launches an app on other simulators without rebuilding
Pairs iPhone and Apple Watch simulators
Auto-refreshes when simulators or apps change
caveats: Requires Xcode 12.0 or later and depends on Xcode command line tools
README does not describe build steps beyond a section heading
